new_statements.quote: 2.3 Tones. There are 4 tones in Va, 1 of which is level and 3 of which are contour. [...] [33] mid-level, [35] mid-rising, [51] high-falling, [21] low-falling [...] No stress patterns have been observed in Va, and intonation patterns have not been researched. 2.4 Syllable structure. The permissible syllable structure of Va, which is a monosyllabic tonal language, is as follows. C(C)V(V)(N/C)T [...] Also, since Va is monosyllabic with isolating morphology, no morphophonemic processes have been observed in the language. Unlike some Angkuic languages such as Muak Sa-aak (Hall 2010), there are no minor syllables (sesquisyllables) in Va.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Northern Va is described as a monosyllabic four-tone language with every syllable carrying a lexical tone and no sesquisyllabic (minor+major) structure; the author reports that no word-stress patterns were observed (and intonation was not studied). I.e. tone, not stress, is the word-prosodic contrast; no stress placement rule is given because none was found.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The author flags the tone values themselves as provisional (whether 33 is 44/55, whether 21 is 11; tone sandhi unstudied, sec. 5 residue). Disyllabic items in the appendix (e.g. lu²¹mo³³ 'stone', tiʔ³³pak⁵¹ '100') are transcribed with a full tone on each syllable and no stress mark.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the word/citation-form level, based on a ~246-270-item elicited wordlist from one Wamo speaker (April 2014); phrase-level prosody explicitly not researched. Preliminary term-paper sketch, not an instrumental study.
new_statements.identity_note: Hsiu (2015) explicitly describes Northern Va (autonym vaʔ⁵¹; Wamo 瓦莫 and neighbouring hamlets of Taihe Administrative Village, Jingxing Township, Mojiang County), which is exactly the variety Glottolog equates with east2776 ('Northern Va of Wamo and surroundings, also known as Eastern Angkuic'). Southern Va (Zhenglong village cluster, ~1,000 older speakers, sesquisyllabic, more conservative) is mentioned but not described; it has no separate glottocode. Not to be confused with Wa/Waic 'Va' (Paraok etc.) or with the Northern Angkuic 'Va/Auva/Alva' lects under U [uuuu1243].

sources.note: Sec. 2.3 (p. 8): Va has 4 tones (33, 35, 51, 21); 'No stress patterns have been observed in Va, and intonation patterns have not been researched.' Sec. 2.4 (pp. 8-9): Va is 'a monosyllabic tonal language', syllable C(C)V(V)(N/C)T, no vowel length, and 'there are no minor syllables (sesquisyllables) in Va'.
